report:
The entire mathematical manuscript passes in its precisely stated scope, relative to the four caller-granted bodies. R/T/C/S were checked for their exact domains and applications; their historical verdicts and author ledgers were not used as certification. They are task assumptions and therefore are excluded from the external-premise list.

One harmless wording correction is needed in Section 3: replace “its maximalization has positive energy defect” with “the original nonmaximal ray has positive energy defect relative to its maximalization.” The maximalized ray itself has zero defect. Equations (15)–(16) already use the correct meaning, so no proof changes are required.

I independently opened the [published BDL paper](https://msp.org/gt/2017/21-5/gt-v21-n5-p08-s.pdf) and read the complete statements and proofs of Propositions 4.4–4.5 and Theorem 4.7, including the surrounding definitions and nonpluripolar-product identification. These are compact Kähler results without projectivity assumptions. The final displayed chord in the Theorem 4.7 proof has reversed endpoint weights; the standard weights follow immediately from its preceding convexity step. This is a harmless typographical correction.

The convention conversion is correct. With v=u/(2π), the currents and probability measures agree, d1 and ordinary energy scale by 1/(2π), and Tγ(u)=2πn AMγ(v). The Ricci and mean-scalar factors then give exactly M=H+T−Ric+S̄E, with entropy coefficient one. The squared-log time is retained from R throughout; no differently calibrated entropy slope is imported. For smooth γ≥0, Proposition 4.5 applies with β=γ and f=0. Decreasing smooth endpoint approximation, granted geodesic continuity, and Proposition 4.4 justify passage to arbitrary E1 segments. Thus the positive contracted-energy convexity used on singular-start rays is actually proved.

Both chord lemmas are sound. For t≥T, the lower chord is f_j(0)/t+(f_j(T)−f_j(0))/T, and the upper bound is f_j(0)/t+ℓ_j. Convergence of initial constants and fixed-time lower convergence give the claimed joint bounds. In the infinite lemma, either one fixed target value is infinite or finite target chords become arbitrarily large. Neither argument assumes convergence of approximant slopes. Subsequences and the diagonal selection j_k≥k, t_k≥k establish the full joint quantifier and the finite-branch uniform-tail formulation. The scalar examples f=−log(1+t), f_j=0 and, separately, f_j=f confirm that these hypotheses imply neither fixed-time equality nor a uniform additive O(1) recession remainder.

The contracted-energy proposition holds for every fixed w∈E1, without an entropy assumption. Its initial constants are the actual finite numbers Tγ(w). R supplies fixed-time d1 convergence and finite, strongly continuous calibrated mixed slopes. Positive-form convexity gives the joint limit; a single fixed decomposition γ=(γ+cω)−cω handles signed forms. In particular, the smooth signed Ricci form requires no positivity assumption. The model slope A^n·ρ_X*[γ]/V matches R’s calibrated mixed-intersection signature; it has no extra n or probability-renormalization factor. Energy affinity gives the asserted joint correction G.

For the finite entropy branch, every approximant has finite entropy at every finite time by R, since both H(w) and its NA entropy are finite. The target enjoys the same conclusion. Hence f_j=M(r_j) and f=M(r) are finite convex functions with the common initial value M(w). Lower semicontinuity supplies exactly the required one-sided fixed-time inequality. The assumed NA entropy convergence, together with mixed-slope continuity, gives convergence of the Mabuchi recession slopes. Applying the finite chord lemma and subtracting the independently established joint G limit proves every entropy limit in (9).

For the infinite branch, the actual start supplies the finite-entropy slice required by R’s classification. The target Mabuchi function is extended convex with finite initial value and recession +∞. Finite-time infinite values are permitted and are handled explicitly by the infinite chord lemma. Its application establishes joint Mabuchi divergence without an approximant entropy-limit hypothesis. The joint G correction remains finite because the target datum is in E1,NA; subtracting it establishes joint entropy divergence. There is no undefined subtraction of two infinite quantities.

The model-sequence consequence uses precisely R’s equation (16): actual relatively Kähler geometric models, strong convergence, and NA entropy convergence for a finite-entropy target. Each model has finite entropy by its finite central-component formula. Their classes may be real and transcendental; no rational bundle or semiampleness is inferred. The rays retain the exact w, including unbounded nonmodel starts. The manuscript constructs no infinite-target model sequence unconditionally. The energy identity retains E(w), and R’s continuity estimate supplies uniform d1 convergence on every bounded time interval.

The boundary comparisons respect the grant domains. T is used only for zero-start finite-height one-branch curve roofs. In the bad-roof diagnostic reconstructed in S, R_j=1/j−1/j²+(Σ_{i=1}^{j−1}1/i)/j³−(j−1)/j⁴ tends to zero, while endpoint mass is 1/j and endpoint distance from the trivial target is (1−1/j)/2. Thus energy and joint entropy recovery do not imply endpoint recovery; the product sequence still recovers the trivial target. C changes an absolute genuine zero-mass endpoint into a minus-infinite placeholder only in its finite-H, CPn, n≥2 scope. S retains its one prescribed singular start and proves relative endpoint collapse with masses j^−k and joint entropy recovery. Neither result supplies arbitrary relative-profile density.

Recognition of a relative ceiling is invoked only when the Legendre level is genuinely psh. No general psh-level assertion is silently assumed. Positive-degree raw masses are never divided by their total mass; the zero extension at a minus-infinite boundary defines neither a current nor a singularity metric, and it does not extend M0. The relative, absolute, and multiplier-ideal envelope definitions are independently matched to [Darvas–Xia–Zhang v3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2302.02541v3). The zero-start polarized log-discrepancy comparison matches the complete statement and proof of [Darvas–Zhang v2, Theorem 10.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2509.15173v2), whose conclusion concerns chordal distance and radial entropy, without asserting relative semiampleness or prescribed closed P profiles. The original supported carrier, multiplicities, discrepancy factors, and real cohomological model meanings agree with R.

Finally, R gives δ=Eα(ψ)−c_u>0 and d1(r(w,ψ)_t,u_t)=tδ for a nonmaximal ray. For any supplied strongly converging maximal model sequence, energy’s Lipschitz inequality proves (16); its bounded-time limit is the maximalization. This establishes only the stated mechanism limitation. No universal approximation obstruction follows.

No fixed-time entropy continuity, general closed-P density, or approximation theorem for all actual rays is claimed or proved. Original P19.2 remains open, and candidate=false is correct.

passages.statement: Darvas–Xia–Zhang, arXiv:2302.02541v3, Section 2.1: on a connected compact Kähler manifold with a smooth closed real big form θ, for genuine u,v∈PSH(X,θ), Pθ[u](v)=(lim_{C→∞}Pθ(u+C,v))*; the absolute envelope uses v=Vθ. The I-envelope is Pθ[u]I(v)=sup{z∈PSH(X,θ): z≤v, I(tz)⊆I(tu) for every t≥0}, where I(tu) is locally generated by holomorphic f for which |f|²e^−tu is integrable.
